questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has a perimeter of $18\text{ cm}$. What is the length of each side?
questions.explanation: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides. Each side is $\frac{18}{3} = 6\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length $5\text{ cm}$, $12\text{ cm}$, and $13\text{ cm}$. What type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: Check using Pythagoras' theorem: $5^2 + 12^2 = 25 + 144 = 169 = 13^2$. Since the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides equals the square of the longest side, it is a right-angled triangle.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of side lengths cannot form a triangle?
questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality, the sum of any two sides must be greater than the third. For $2, 3, 6$: $2 + 3 = 5 < 6$, so these lengths cannot form a triangle.
